name: Ongoing and foreground service notifications
plain: A notification the person cannot easily swipe away that shows background work is running.
meaning: It makes background activity visible. Android 14 let people swipe most of these away, but the Task Manager (Android 13+) still lists the foreground app.

android.prompt_ui: Foreground service notification; Task Manager lists active apps (Android 13+)
android.persistence: Visible while the service runs; Android 14 lets users dismiss most
android.note: Android 12 delays display of non-essential FGS notifications by about 10 s

ios.api_surface: Live Activities; Control Center now playing; location blue pill
ios.note: iOS has no generic persistent notification; use of background modes shows system indicators instead

limits.headline: Can show a notification you cannot easily swipe away while background work runs
limits.user_action: You start something long, like music, a download or navigation
can: Show an ongoing alert while a background service is running
Appear in Android's Task Manager list of active apps on Android 13 or newer
Show a Live Activity or audio indicator on iPhone instead
cannot: Hide that the app is running on Android
Show every foreground alert right away; Android 12 delays unimportant ones by about 10 seconds
Make a generic permanent alert on iPhone, which has none
limits.reach_label: While work runs, visible to you
limits.differs: Android shows a persistent foreground notification. iPhone shows system indicators or Live Activities instead.

story.what_it_is: A notification that stays put to show an app is doing work in the background.

marketing.name: Foreground services
marketing.pitch: Google documents the foreground service notification as the visible sign that an app is doing ongoing work.

story.for_you: You see a music player or a navigation card that does not go away. It is a clear sign that something is running, and on Android you can check the Task Manager.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to keep tasks alive and avoid being killed by the system. It can also be a trick if an app hides behind a persistent notification.

use_cases.example: A player keeps a notification with play and pause while you work.
A navigation app shows the next turn in the notification.
A run tracker keeps a notification so you can pause from the shade.
A call app keeps an ongoing call notification with a hang up button.
A game download shows a progress notification until it is done.
A security app keeps a notification that says Home mode active.
A VPN app shows a key icon while it protects your traffic.

story.android_note: From Android 14 people can swipe away most of these. Task Manager lists active apps from Android 13.
story.ios_note: iOS has no generic persistent notification. It shows system indicators for audio or location instead.

technical_bounds: Android 12 defers display; Android 14 can be swiped away

abuse: Hiding in a persistent notification to avoid kills

history.change: Foreground Services Task Manager lists active apps with stop button
Users can dismiss most ongoing foreground service notifications
FGS notification deferred about 10 s for short work
